section.title: The Neighbours Nobody Excavated
section.form_description: One enthusiasm followed all the way down. The narrator opens on a subject they love and know cold — how a mass relay actually throws a ship, the grammar of their homeworld's oldest language, the breeding lines behind a varren pit — and talks it out well past where a listener would have stopped them, then follows a seam into the next subject and the next. An infodump, but a personal one: every fact is here because the narrator went and got it, and why they cared runs under the telling — the childhood that started it, the person who taught them, the love and the plain curiosity of it. Sections are subjects, each opening where the last one's tangent left off.
section.form_note: Rewritten after feedback. The brief is one enthusiasm talked out at length, which is tunnel; but the spine is topical and associative, not Shepard's playthrough. The order is a chain of thoughts, each section opening from an object, a feeling or an aside in the one before (a dated fragment -> the ruins the Protheans themselves dug up -> the empire -> the neighbours nobody excavated -> a goddess who was a guise -> what other species made of them -> the Mars cache -> a message meant for someone else's mind -> her own dig -> the fall and the shelters -> the Crucible -> the cycles before -> the arithmetic of a cycle -> what to leave). Nothing runs in game order; Shepard's encounters (Eden Prime beacon, Therum, Feros, Ilos, Thessia, Javik, the Leviathan trail) appear as evidence or anecdote inside a topical section, and where Liara was not there (Eden Prime beacon, the Leviathan trail; Feros and the Presidium hanar dispute she did attend, per Thomas) she draws on Shepard and on her own Shadow Broker network (she is the Broker), saying which source she is using, not merely asking Shepard. Canon kept: Shepard was marked by the beacon, Javik came aboard, the Leviathan DLC and Thessia as recorded; Legion/Tali branches and the ending are not touched, and the talk stops short of the final choice. Pre-Prothean material comes only from corpus pages (Inusannon, thoi'han/Eingana, the Leviathan of Dis, the Leviathans, the Crucible design history) and is hedged in her voice: the corpus dates the Inusannon at 127,000 years and the Protheans at 68,000-48,000 BCE, which does not fit a tidy fifty-thousand-year cycle, and she should worry at that rather than resolve it. target_words is pinned at 9000 (a one-hour spoken lecture at roughly 150 words a minute, pauses included).

required_facts.fact: In 2186, during the Reaper War, Cerberus occupied the Alliance colony of Eden Prime after discovering an intact Prothean stasis pod buried in a bunker complex that had sheltered Protheans 50,000 years earlier. Cerberus abducted able-bodied colonists under the cover story that they were doing safe manual labour at a research camp, using increased food rations to quiet complaints, while it researched how to open the pod. A local resistance movement formed to fight the occupation. Alerted by Liara T'Soni to the archaeological find, Commander Shepard landed with a squad, fought through Cerberus troops, Atlas mechs and Nemesis snipers, and raised the buried artifact lift. Shepard recovered the stasis pod and revived its occupant: Javik, the last living Prothean, an "Avatar of Vengeance" and military commander from the final cycle of the war against the Reapers. Javik joined the Normandy as a squad member and living repository of Prothean history. In the parallel objective "Eden Prime: Resistance Movement," Shepard could gather three pieces of Cerberus intel from colony terminals, revealing that Cerberus had thinned its northern troops while faking strength, and that Dr. William Cambiata was a Cerberus mole inside the resistance whom Cerberus planned to let "escape" as a staged hero. Collecting all three drove Cerberus off Eden Prime and boosted the Eden Prime war asset; the objective became permanently unavailable once the lift was raised.
Javik, the last living Prothean, was revived from stasis and joined Shepard's squad
Cerberus lost its Prothean research site on Eden Prime
The abduction of Eden Prime colonists by Cerberus was exposed
Gathering the resistance intel drove Cerberus off the colony and improved the Eden Prime war asset
Javik provided firsthand knowledge of the Protheans, the Reapers and the Crucible-era conflict

During the Reaper extermination of the Protheans, roughly 50,000 years before Commander Shepard's era, a fortified bunker complex on the world later called Eden Prime served as a refuge where Prothean survivors gathered to enter cryogenic stasis, intending to emerge after the Reapers withdrew into dark space and rebuild the Prothean Empire. The facility was overseen by Victory, a Prothean Virtual Intelligence that appeared as a holographic Prothean and could project itself anywhere in the base, keeping the bunker's commander, the soldier Javik, apprised of the battle. As Collector ground troops closed in, Javik ordered Victory to broadcast the stasis-readiness signal to all lifepods; Victory noted that refugees were still en route, and Javik dismissed their loss as a necessary sacrifice. Victory then reported that Reaper forces had destroyed roughly 300,000 lifepods - about a third of the surviving Protheans - and that the northside bulkhead could not be sealed. With the bunker about to be overrun, Victory ordered Javik into his stasis pod and triggered a neutron bombardment, refusing his request for more time and turning his own words back on him: "Their sacrifice will be honored in the coming empire." The blast destroyed the attacking Reaper forces but damaged the base's sensors, making automatic reawakening impossible; the survivors could only be revived manually if a later civilization discovered the facility. Over Javik's protests, Victory triaged the bunker's dwindling power, eventually cutting power to every stasis pod except Javik's and appointing him the voice of the Prothean people before he entered stasis. Every other Prothean in the bunker died. Javik slept until Shepard's team unearthed and revived him on Eden Prime in 2186, making him the last living Prothean.
Roughly 300,000 Prothean lifepods are destroyed by Reaper forces at the bunker
Victory's neutron bombardment destroys the attacking Reaper forces but cripples the base's auto-revival sensors
Power is cut to every stasis pod except Javik's; all other Protheans in the bunker die
Javik is designated the voice of the Prothean people and sealed in stasis for 50,000 years
The intact stasis pod is later found by Cerberus and Shepard on Eden Prime, yielding Javik as the last living Prothean

canon.statement: Shepard was born in Normandie in France, parentless, ran with a gang as a child and had a drug problem before Anderson pulled him into N7.
canon.overrides: Earthborn background as the wiki describes it

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. The Normandy crash-landed, there's been no word, and the crew takes that silence to mean he's dead: there's no body and no report. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. There is still no body, so no burial. Shepard's lover puts his name on the Normandy's memorial wall, or chooses not to, and the crew holds a night of remembrance for him: to celebrate the man he was, to mourn him, or both.
canon.overrides: shepard_fate = Dead (synthesis) stated as settled fact

canon.statement: Shepard never had a first name. "Shepard" started as a mocking nickname the Tenth Street Reds gave him for his knack with people. He only took a surname because Alliance enlistment required one, and he kept that one as a screw-you to the Reds.
canon.overrides: Earthborn Shepard as the wiki describes it (first name player-chosen, surname by birth)

canon.statement: Shepard got clean of drugs but never stopped loving alcohol and parties. Jack thinks the good-guy act is just that, an act: in her telling he has turned up at every bar in the galaxy and calls each one his favorite, and he drinks and dances every time. He even did it on Omega, where somebody could have poisoned him. She calls him a drunk and a dumbass, and she's fond of him.

scenes.title: Waking the Last Prothean on Eden Prime
scenes.when: 2186, Priority: Eden Prime (From Ashes), after the Normandy left the Citadel
scenes.where: the Cerberus-occupied Prothean dig site on Eden Prime, Exodus Cluster

beats.text: Alliance command reported that Cerberus had attacked and occupied Eden Prime to secure a major Prothean artifact. Shepard infiltrated the colony with Liara T'Soni as a mandatory squadmate; on the shuttle in the team talked about the last time Shepard had been to Eden Prime.

A cutscene at the dig site revealed that Cerberus had excavated a living Prothean held in stasis, and had damaged his lifepod during the dig, leaving his life signs unstable. Liara worked out that opening the pod without killing him needed both a command signal to end stasis and a safe physical method of opening it, each being researched at a separate Cerberus laboratory.

At the lab terminals Shepard's eyes glowed green while watching Prothean footage of the Reaper invasion 50,000 years earlier — the VI Victory sealing bunker bulkheads, some 300,000 lifepods destroyed, the stasis-readiness signal broadcast while refugees were still trying to reach shelter. Liara saw only static, and deduced that Shepard's exposure to the Prothean Cipher on Feros (or the Eden Prime beacon in a non-imported game) let the Commander read the images.
Shepard returned to the pod, transmitted the command signal, and held the site against waves of Cerberus troops and an Atlas mech.

The pod opened. Shepard spoke with the Prothean on the planet and again back aboard the Normandy; he introduced himself as Javik and joined the squad, found afterward in the port cargo hold. He stayed out of combat until Priority: Palaven was done, saying he was still recovering from stasis.

evidence.text:
Mass Effect 3: From Ashes was a DLC pack for Mass Effect 3, accidentally revealed February 21, 2012 when Microsoft made it available over Xbox Live, and released alongside the game on March 6, 2012. In its story, Cerberus attacks Eden Prime and takes over a human colony while stretched-thin Alliance forces cannot respond; intel shows Cerberus is after a Prothean artifact it has found, and Shepard infiltrates the colony to recover it. The artifact proves to be Javik, the last surviving Prothean, who joins as a permanent squad member and provides lore about the last days of the Prothean empire before the Reapers wiped out the species.

Content comprised the squadmate Javik, two missions (Priority: Eden Prime and Eden Prime: Resistance Movement), the Prothean Particle Rifle, and a new alternate outfit for every squadmate. It was free with the N7 Collector's Edition and Digital Deluxe Edition, sold separately for 800 BioWare Points or $10.00 USD, included with the Wii U Special Edition, and is part of Mass Effect Legendary Edition.

evidence.text: In Prothean society, there were many "Avatars", Protheans who embodied a single virtue for the society. Javik is one of those Avatars, and his virtue is Vengeance. According to Javik, he was the last of the warriors of the Prothean Empire, born in the midst of the war with the Reapers, a war the Protheans were losing. The Citadel had already fallen long before he was born, and his first memories were of seeing his planet on fire during a Reaper assault. Javik was to be the leader of approximately one million warriors who were to survive the cull via stasis in an underground bunker on Eden Prime. His mission was simple: outlast the invasion in stasis, and once he was awoken, lead the others in a campaign to reclaim the galaxy. Unfortunately, indoctrinated traitors in their ranks foiled that plan, betraying the bunker's location to the Reapers. As hundreds of thousands of Protheans in stasis were slaughtered by the Collectors, the supervising VI Victory was forced to initiate a neutron purge to clear out the facility while Javik took refuge in his own stasis pod. Unfortunately, the purge compromised the bunker's sensor systems, rendering automatic reactivation of the remaining stasis pods impossible. Since Javik now had to remain in stasis indefinitely until a new culture discovered the facility, Victory determined that power needs for the last intact pods had to be triaged. In the end, only Javik would be reawakened.

evidence.text: |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | **Victory** was a Prothean VI overseer of a bunker facility on Eden Prime. During the Reaper invasion of the planet 50,000 years before the present, Victory kept its base commander Javik apprised of then\-ongoing threats to the bunker. With extinction at the hands of the Reapers seemingly inevitable, Prothean survivors have gathered at the facility. It was here that the survivors hoped to enter cryogenic stasis, emerging after the Reapers have reentered dark space to rebuild the Prothean Empire. As Collector ground troops closed in on the facility, Javik instructed Victory to broadcast the readiness signal to all lifepods. Victory reminded Javik of the refugees who have yet to reach the bunker, which Javik dismissed as a necessary sacrifice. As Javik and others fought to seal off the base, Victory informed Javik that Reaper forces have destroyed approximately 300,000 lifepods—a third of the Protheans. Victory later notified Javik that the northside bulkhead cannot be sealed, and relayed Javik's orders for all forces to converge there. The bunker soon fell in danger of being overrun despite the defenders' efforts. With no other options remaining, Victory ordered Javik into his stasis pod and set off the neutron bombardment. It denied Javik's protests for a few more minutes' reprieve for his men and other online pods to safely escape the purge, as it used Javik's own words against him: "Their sacrifice will be honored in the coming empire." The blast eliminated the Reaper threat but damaged the base's sensors and made it impossible for automatic reawakening. This meant that the remaining Protheans can only be reawakened manually when a new culture discovers the facility, which may result in a shortage of power to the stasis pods. Over Javik's protests to not shut down any pods, Victory said it will triage the base's power supply appropriately. As Javik is the only known Prothean survivor, it would appear that Victory was eventually forced to cut power to all pods except for Javik's. It appointed him as the voice of their people shortly before Javik went into stasis. Victory's ultimate fate is unknown. If Commander Shepard reawakens Javik in 2186, Victory is neither seen nor heard from except in flashbacks induced by contact with Prothean data and Javik himself. Unlike other degraded Prothean VIs encountered by Shepard from 2183 onwards, Victory appears just like a holographic Prothean. It can be projected anywhere in the facility, and like Vendetta it can simulate ambulatory movement when necessary. The other known Prothean VIs, Vigil and Vendetta, were created using personality imprints from actual Protheans. It is unknown if this is the case with Victory and if so, from whose personality imprints it is based.
evidence.for_key: Javik last Prothean bunker Eden Prime

evidence.text:
Victory was a Prothean VI that served as overseer of a bunker facility on Eden Prime. During the Reaper invasion 50,000 years before the present, Victory kept the base commander Javik apprised of ongoing threats. Prothean survivors gathered at the facility hoping to enter cryogenic stasis and emerge after the Reapers withdrew into dark space to rebuild the Prothean Empire.

As Collector ground troops closed in, Javik ordered Victory to broadcast the readiness signal to all lifepods. Victory reminded him of refugees still en route, which Javik dismissed as a necessary sacrifice. Victory reported that Reaper forces had destroyed roughly 300,000 lifepods, a third of the Protheans, and that the northside bulkhead could not be sealed. With the bunker about to be overrun, Victory ordered Javik into his stasis pod and triggered a neutron bombardment, denying his request for a few more minutes for his men to escape and using his own words against him: "Their sacrifice will be honored in the coming empire."

The blast destroyed the Reaper threat but damaged the base's sensors, making automatic reawakening impossible; the surviving Protheans could only be revived manually when a new culture discovered the facility, risking a power shortage to the stasis pods. Over Javik's protests, Victory said it would triage the base's power supply, and it eventually cut power to all pods except Javik's, appointing him the voice of their people before he entered stasis. Victory's ultimate fate is unknown; if Shepard reawakened Javik in 2186, Victory appeared only in flashbacks. Unlike other degraded Prothean VIs, Victory appeared as a holographic Prothean and could project anywhere in the facility. Whether, like Vigil and Vendetta, it was based on a real Prothean's personality imprint is unknown.
evidence.for_key: Javik last Prothean bunker Eden Prime

evidence.text: Ilos was not the only place where Protheans tried to survive in stasis. Nearly one million Prothean warriors and their commander, Javik, were stored in cryogenic lifepods in a bunker facility on Eden Prime. Javik's mission was to lead the warriors in rebuilding the Prothean Empire once the Reaper threat had passed. Before the facility could be sealed, however, indoctrinated traitors leaked its existence to the Reapers. Hundreds of thousands of stasis pods were destroyed in the attack on the facility, killing their occupants. To preserve the few remaining survivors, the facility's VI, Victory, initiated a neutron bombardment to purge Reaper forces. The bombardment also severely damaged the facility and rendered the systems responsible for automatically awakening the Protheans from stasis inoperable. As Javik's survival was a priority, Victory was forced to divert power from the remaining stasis pods to keep Javik's pod working as long as possible in the hope that future civilizations would discover it and revive him. Over 50,000 years after Javik entered stasis, Commander Shepard may discover and activate his pod. With his race destroyed and his mission failed, Javik believes his only remaining purpose is to wreak vengeance on the Reapers by joining Commander Shepard. During the Reaper invasion in 2186, some of the surviving Collectors may be freed from Reaper control through subversion by the ancient race called Leviathans. These "awakened" Collectors are the last embers of the extinct Prothean race, also embodying the Prothean virtue of vengeance.
evidence.for_key: Javik last Prothean bunker Eden Prime

evidence.text: The Collectors arose during the closing years of the Reapers' harvest of the Protheans. The Reapers subjected captured Protheans to extensive genetic experimentation and implanted them with cybernetics. Eventually, the end result was the Collectors, a race of completely subservient creatures that the Reapers could remotely use as tools. Collectors were deployed against the last Protheans at the end of their cycle. A Prothean plan to place one million of their kind in stasis in bunkers on Eden Prime to wait out the Reapers and then rebuild their empire failed after indoctrinated agents alerted the Reapers. While Reapers razed the Prothean surface cities, Collector Drones infiltrated the bunker system and destroyed hundreds of thousands of occupied stasis pods. In the end, only the Prothean Javik would survive the onslaught. Once the Reapers concluded their harvest, they departed the galaxy and returned to dark space, while the Collectors retreated beyond the Omega 4 Relay. |  | ***“I know when something's not right.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Incursion** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  | ***“I said get back!”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Redemption** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  | ***“Salvation comes with a cost.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Ascension** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
Javik was the only known survivor of the ancient Prothean race, revived in 2186 after more than 50,000 years in stasis and driven by vengeance against the Reapers for his people's extinction. He was written mainly by John Dombrow and added through the From Ashes DLC, fully integrated into the Legendary Edition.

In Prothean society, "Avatars" each embodied a single virtue; Javik's was Vengeance. Born mid-war on a galaxy already losing to the Reapers, he was to lead roughly one million warriors who would outlast the invasion in stasis in an underground bunker on Eden Prime, then reclaim the galaxy. Indoctrinated traitors betrayed the bunker to the Reapers, and the Collectors slaughtered the sleeping Protheans. The supervising VI Victory initiated a neutron purge that damaged the bunker's sensors, making mass reactivation impossible; power was triaged so that only Javik would wake.

Commander Shepard and Liara T'Soni uncovered and opened his pod on Eden Prime while investigating Cerberus. Javik attacked them on waking, then agreed to join the fight to destroy the Reapers. Through touch he could read biological memories and instantly learned human language. He held imperialist, social-Darwinist views: he preached the "Cosmic Imperative," dismissed mercy, morality, and friendship as weakness, believed allies were merely resources, and thought the modern "primitive" races should be forced to help rather than asked. He refused to use names, referring to people by species or job. He took Grunt's former quarters aboard the Normandy and clashed repeatedly with the crew, especially EDI, whose capacity for choice he found troubling, and Liara, whose persistent questions and asari heritage he needled. He recounted Prothean history with the rachni (bred as weapons), the zha and synthetic zha'til, the densorin, and the asari, whom the Protheans secretly "guided" as this cycle's best hope, a claim that nearly provoked Liara to violence over events on Thessia.

If persuaded to use his Prothean Echo Shard, Javik relived hunting down and killing his own indoctrinated crew, concluding that war is atrocity committed for survival. Asked what he would do after the war, he might choose to return to the Cronian Nebula to take his own life and rejoin his comrades, or, if reconciled with Liara, co-author a book with her titled "Journeys with the Prothean," or live among the hanar on Kahje. In the Citadel DLC he starred alongside Shepard in "Blasto 7: Blasto Goes to War." If Shepard lacked sufficient forces, Javik could be killed by Harbinger in the final push; if he survived, he honored Shepard at the Memorial Wall. "Javik" derives from the Hindi word for "biological" or "organic."
evidence.for_key: Javik last Prothean bunker Eden Prime

evidence.text:
Priority: Eden Prime was a Mass Effect 3 mission added by the Mass Effect 3: From Ashes DLC (included by default in Legendary Edition), available after Priority: The Citadel I and completable any time before Priority: Cerberus Headquarters. An Alliance message reported that Cerberus had attacked and occupied the Eden Prime colony to secure a major Prothean artifact, and tasked Shepard with infiltrating the colony to recover it. Liara T'Soni was a mandatory squadmate, and the opposition was heavily shielded Cerberus infantry, turrets, and an Atlas mech.

On landing, the team learned that Cerberus had excavated a living Prothean held in stasis, whose lifepod had been damaged during the dig, leaving his life signs unstable. Opening the pod without killing him required both a command signal to end stasis mode and a safe physical method of opening it, each being researched at a separate Cerberus laboratory. Shepard fought through the colony to both labs. evidence.text:
A Virtual Intelligence (VI) was a sophisticated program designed to make computer systems easier to use. VIs were distinct from artificial intelligences such as the geth: they only assisted users and processed data, and although they appeared intelligent, they were not self-aware, merely the product of clever programming. This greatly reduced, though did not eliminate, the risk of a VI exceeding its intended function or rebelling against its creators. Some VIs carried "personality imprints," basing their behavior, speech, and appearance on specific individuals, though it was illegal to model a VI on a living person. The quarians had been attempting to make their "ancestor VIs" truly intelligent to achieve a kind of virtual immortality when the geth rebellion halted most synthetic-intelligence research.

VIs varied widely by deployment. They handled extranet search queries, served as tour guides like the Citadel VI Avina, and managed lab and database work like Mira on Noveria. Humans and elcor both used VIs extensively in military operations to process status reports and react faster than organics, with elcor VIs instantly selecting among millions of pre-designed combat gambits. Many armor upgrades used VI enhancements to optimize combat performance or dispense medi-gel, and the L4 biotic implant used VI technology to monitor the user's brain waves and adapt in real time.

A VI that deviated from its programming due to software errors or malicious tampering was called a "rogue VI." Such a VI was not self-aware; going rogue was akin to a software malfunction that caused the VI to fail its function or interpret its duties dangerously. Notable incidents included a Systems Alliance VI at a Luna training facility that went rogue after scientists tried to convert it into a controllable AI and triggered the facility's weapons; the VI on Jarrahe Station that engaged a lockdown killing all scientists aboard; and a Cerberus project on Aite where an experimental hybrid VI became a virus that seized a research facility and its living geth test subjects, killing nearly all personnel present.

Notable VIs listed included Avina (Citadel and Nexus information), the ExoGeni VI on Feros, the geth-created Geth VI studying the Reapers, the rogue Alliance VI Hannibal on Luna, the Shadow Broker's Info Drone "Glyph," the Andromeda ark VI "K" (Keelah Si'yah), the last surviving Ancestor VI Liat'Nir, Mira at Peak 15 on Noveria, the Cerberus Overlord VI on Aite, the Shepard VI, the Prothean VI Vendetta on Thessia, the Prothean VI Victory on Eden Prime, and the Prothean VI Vigil on Ilos.

evidence.text: This Codex update, added with the Bring Down the Sky DLC, contained a single Secondary entry on translation technology. It noted that humanity remained linguistically divided across languages such as Spanish, Mandarin, Arabic, and Swahili, and that every alien race had a similarly broad range of languages and dialects. Most individuals knew only their mother tongue and relied on machine translation, which a few hundred credits of equipment (handheld PDAs, computers in clothing or jewelry, or sub-dermal implants) could provide in seamless real time; without it, galactic trade and culture would not exist. Governments distributed subsidized translation software updated over the public extranet, often as travelers approached spaceport customs, and even the isolationist batarians supplied up-to-date glossaries, widely assumed to be so they could keep exporting propaganda. Speaking without machine aid was still considered broad-minded and practical, children often took courses in alien languages, and most races could manage the simplified artificial "trade tongue." Some species depended on machine translation entirely: the hanar could not reproduce the spoken language of any humanoid species, and other races could not reproduce hanar bioluminescence without mechanical aid. Newly discovered or obscure races had no machine translation until linguists had studied them.

evidence.text: The Horse Head Nebula was a star cluster of mostly uninhabited, barely-surveyed planets with modest resourcing prospects. Cerberus maintained major operations in the cluster: Minuteman Station was located there in 2185, and by 2186 the organization's headquarters (Cronos Station) and at least one outpost lay in out-of-the-way positions within the nebula. Missions set here included the Noveria arc in Mass Effect and Priority: Cerberus Headquarters and N7: Cerberus Fighter Base in Mass Effect 3. The real-world nebula is Barnard 33 in IC 434, first identified by Williamina Fleming in 1888; Mass Effect 3 renders the name "Horsehead Nebula" without the space. After acquiring the Normandy SR-2, the Minuteman Station and its surrounding cluster became inaccessible.

evidence.text: The Protheans' belief that they could hold their own against machine intelligence was shattered with the arrival of the Reapers in approximately 48,000 BCE, who were far more advanced than the machines the Protheans had been battling. They were caught completely off\-guard by the scale and rapidity of the assault. The Reapers entered the galaxy through the Citadel, instantly decapitating the Protheans' government and disrupting the mass relay network, isolating Prothean systems from one another. Worse, records on the Citadel provided the Reapers with access to all of the Protheans' census data and star charts, allowing them to effectively track every Prothean in the galaxy. The Protheans' greatest strength, their unified empire, proved to be their downfall. As the Protheans were united under the leadership of a single governing species with a series of subordinate races, the Reapers were able to quickly undermine the Prothean hierarchy and cause Prothean forces to become scattered when their ruling body had been compromised. In addition, as all the races within the Empire conformed to a single military doctrine, they proved unable to adapt when the Reapers identified and exploited their weaknesses. While their domain crumbled, the Protheans were powerless to defend other races from the Reapers' predations. They ceased all study of primitive species in the hope that the Reapers would deem them too primitive for harvest. It was hoped that some Protheans would survive the Reapers' purge and go on to unite these species to create a new empire. The Protheans' primitive subjects survived and went on to become the present cycle's dominant ones. Other races subjugated under them, however, weren't as lucky. The densorin, a race who had mastered sciences beyond even the Protheans' understanding, attempted to pacify the Reapers by sacrificing their children to them, but this only allowed the Reapers to destroy them more quickly. The zha'til, symbiotic AIs that had been created by a race called the zha to keep themselves alive on their dying homeworld, were subjugated by the Reapers and formed hostile mechanical swarms. They became such a threat that the Protheans were forced to obliterate the zha'til entirely by sending the star of the zha's home system into supernova. Over the next several centuries, the Protheans fought the Reapers from system to system, world to world, and city to city. If necessary, whole colonies were sacrificed and abandoned to the Reapers; while the Reapers concentrated on subsuming the inhabitants of those colonies, the Protheans had time to regroup. In the long run, however, this strategy was extremely costly, depriving the remaining Protheans of whatever infrastructure and manpower they had given up. Inexorably, the Reapers conquered, enslaved, or destroyed Prothean\-controlled planets. Growing desperate, some Protheans made repeated offers of surrender to the Reapers, but these were always met with silence. In addition to the overt threat of the Reapers, the Protheans had to increasingly deal with enemies from within their own ranks. Indoctrinated Protheans acted as sleeper agents for the Reapers, infiltrating and swiftly betraying their own kind and revealing the Protheans' dwindling hiding places and carefully\-laid plans to survive the destruction. At some point the Protheans learned of the cycles of galactic destruction through studying the ruins of other extinguished civilizations. Plans for the Crucible, which was based on designs left behind by previous civilizations, were discovered, and the Protheans set about to building one of their own. In the course of the Crucible's construction, some Protheans came to believe that the Reapers could be controlled with the device, but inevitably fell prey to indoctrination as well in their attempts to harness Reaper technology. They sabotaged the Crucible, robbing the Protheans of their last hope to defeat the Reapers. After centuries of careful, systematic work, the Reapers had killed or enslaved every Prothean in the galaxy, and stripped their worlds of resources. Removing all traces of their presence, the Reapers then retreated through the Citadel into dark space and sealed it behind them.

evidence.text:
The Protheans were an ancient race that vanished roughly 50,000 years ago after building a galaxy-wide empire. They were long credited with creating the Citadel and the mass relays, though in truth they only inherited that Reaper technology. Anthropoidal in form, they had two pairs of dual-pupiled eyes, three pairs of nostrils, a layered head carapace, three-fingered hands, and a flanging voice like turians. A unique trait was an experiential exchange system: by touch, a Prothean could absorb another's memories, skills, or language. They had quad-strand DNA, some resistance to low radiation, and at least some members wielded potent biotics.

After achieving spaceflight, the Protheans discovered ruins of the earlier inusannon and learned mass effect physics, gaining a centuries-long secret advantage. Facing a hostile machine intelligence, they decided all organic life must unite under their rule; resisting species were conquered and assimilated, coming to call themselves "Prothean." United, they held off the machines in the Metacon War. They observed and cultivated primitive species including asari, hanar, humans, quarians, salarians and turians, intending eventually to offer them the "choice" of joining the empire.

The Reapers arrived around 48,000 BCE, entering through the Citadel, decapitating the government, disrupting the relay network, and using Citadel census data to hunt every Prothean. Their unified empire and single military doctrine became fatal weaknesses. Indoctrinated Protheans acted as sleeper agents. Subject races like the densorin and the AI zha'til were destroyed; the Protheans themselves annihilated the zha'til by sending a star supernova. Some Protheans built a Crucible from designs left by prior civilizations, but indoctrinated builders sabotaged it. After centuries the Reapers killed or enslaved every Prothean and withdrew into dark space.

Survivors persisted in stasis. On Ilos, the Conduit research team under Ksad Ishan went dark; the VI Vigil cut power to non-essential pods until only about a dozen scientists remained, who later used the Conduit to reach the Citadel and alter the keepers' signal to trap the Reapers. On Eden Prime, nearly a million warriors and their commander Javik were stored; traitors betrayed the site, most pods were destroyed, and the VI Victory kept only Javik's pod alive. Shepard could revive Javik in 2186. Meanwhile the Reapers repurposed captured Protheans into the Collectors, directed by Harbinger to abduct humans for a Human-Reaper.

The Protheans held evolution, the "Cosmic Imperative," as the universe's driving force. Their influence shaped the asari (uplifted as a possible failsafe), humans (via the Mars archive) and the hanar, who worship them as the "Enkindlers." Notable Protheans included Javik, avatar of vengeance, and the guides Janiri and Lucen of asari myth. Prothean tech included mind-to-mind beacons, memory shards, indoctrination detection, kinetic barrier grids, the Particle Rifle, the flagship Penumbra Apex, and the Conduit.

evidence.text:
The Mu Relay was a mass relay lost roughly four thousand years before the events of Mass Effect. It was the only relay linking to the Pangaea Expanse and the former Prothean colony of Ilos. A nearby supernova pushed the relay out of its orbit without damaging it, then swathed it in hot gas and dust, making it undetectable because scanners cannot pick up "cold" objects in interstellar space.

The enveloping nebula lay in rachni-controlled space. Matriarch Benezia explained to Commander Shepard that the fiercely territorial rachni, seeking to close all routes into their space, eventually located the relay through sheer numbers of spacefaring ships. When the krogan exterminated the rachni, the coordinates were thought lost forever, but the Rachni Queen resurrected by Binary Helix carried them in genetic memory. Benezia passed the coordinates to Shepard, though Saren Arterius had already obtained them. Because shifting borders now placed the Mu Relay in the Terminus Systems, the Council refused to send the Citadel Fleet through it to Ilos for fear of starting a war, leaving the stealth-equipped SSV Normandy as the only ship able to reach the relay secretly. The relay was likely named after the fabled lost continent of Mu.

evidence.text: The **densorin** were a race that existed at the time of the Protheans. At some point, they fought a war against the oravores. When the Reapers invaded the galaxy, the densorin attempted to pacify them by sacrificing their children to them, but this only allowed the Reapers to destroy the densorin more quickly. The densorin are known to have studied celestial mechanics and morphological simulations of galactic language, topics beyond the understanding of even the Protheans.

evidence.text: The **oravores** were a spacefaring race that existed at the time of the Protheans. When they attacked the asari homeworld of Thessia to gain control of its vast resources, the Protheans stopped them. This event would later be remembered in asari mythology as when the goddess Athame wielded her sword against jealous gods who threatened the asari. The oravores also fought a war against the densorin.

evidence.text: Sometime before assaulting the main Cerberus Headquarters, Shepard receives a mission from Hackett with orders to meet with Dr. Garrett Bryson on the Citadel to search for leads that can help with the war against the Reapers. During this time period, Javik offers a couple of insights relating to their quarry. After the attempt to locate Dr. Bryson's associate Dr. Garneau, Javik tells Shepard that he witnessed many strange things in his war, such as a settlement of densorin studying complex sciences beyond their understanding. At the time, he thought they were crazy, but having seen what happened on the Mahavid asteroid, he can only wonder. After the rescue of Dr. Ann Bryson, Dr. Bryson's daughter, Javik states that if the Leviathan is really a Reaper defector, then it is also a traitor, for traitors among the enemy can't be trusted. If it could betray its own kind, Javik could only imagine what it could do to Shepard. Shepard succeeds in persuading the Leviathans to join the war effort. Onboard the Normandy Javik reveals he's been studying human religion, and comments that the Leviathans deserve the same fate as the Devil for their involvement in creating the Reapers. He compares the abyss Shepard found the Leviathans hiding in to Hell and he hopes they never leave it.

evidence.text: The asari arose on Thessia, a rich world with abundant quantities of element zero that caused much of life on Thessia to exhibit biotic tendencies. Instrumental to the rise of asari civilization was the intervention of the Protheans. Upon discovering the asari, the Protheans crafted the guise of Athame, a benevolent goddess who imparted gifts of wisdom to the asari through her guides Janiri and Lucen, a deception that allowed the Protheans to rapidly accelerate asari development. The Protheans also genetically altered the asari to grant them biotic capabilities, and defended Thessia from an asteroid strike and the resource\-hungry oravores. When the Protheans departed, they left a single beacon on Thessia, around which the asari later built a lavish temple devoted to Athame. This beacon contained Vendetta, a Prothean VI, and over the following centuries was the source of countless technological advances that allowed the asari to eventually become the most powerful race in the galaxy. The beacon's existence became a closely\-held state secret, as its revelation would have discredited the virtually universal belief that the asari attained such heights on their own merit. By 2183 CE, few outside the highest echelons of the asari government were aware of the part the Protheans played in asari history. 30,000 years prior to the modern era, the asari developed their equivalent of automobiles. Barely any artifacts from this period survived, even as museum pieces.

evidence.text: The Reapers believe they are preserving life. Their reasoning: if organic life keeps advancing and building machines, those machines will eventually exterminate all organics. To prevent that, the Reapers wipe out advanced civilizations every 50,000 years — the harvest. They let species rise using tools the Reapers secretly built (the Citadel and the mass relays), then return and destroy them — but preserve their minds inside new Reapers, which the Reapers regard as a twisted form of immortality. Their goal is to run this cycle forever as the only way to stop total extinction, despite the endless destruction it causes.

evidence.page: Reaper Classes and Sizes (Part 1) — Origin, Purpose, and Ground Forces
evidence.text:
Part 1 of a hand-corrected survey of Reaper types, covering what the Reapers are, their origin, the logic of the harvest, and their ground forces and small constructs. The Reapers were described as gigantic biomechanical machines partly built from living beings, resembling space squids or cuttlefish and ranging in size from a large building to a mountain. Each Reaper housed the fused minds of billions of individuals from a harvested species inside a machine body.

Their origin was traced to roughly a billion years ago, when a race called the Leviathans ruled the galaxy and built a super-intelligent AI to solve the recurring conflict between organic life and the synthetic machines organics create. The AI concluded that permanent control of all life, including the Leviathans, was the only solution. It turned on its makers, wiped out most of them, and used their bodies and minds to build the first Reaper, later known as Harbinger. The process was repeated on other species once they reached a threshold of advancement, producing more Reapers over millions of years.

The harvest was presented as the Reapers' method of preservation: they let civilizations rise using the Citadel and mass relays, which the Reapers secretly built, then returned every 50,000 years to destroy advanced civilizations while preserving their minds inside new Reapers, a form of immortality by the Reapers' reckoning.

The page then catalogs Reaper ground troops and small constructs: husks (bodies converted on dragon's-teeth spikes into cybernetic zombies, the most common troops); cannibals (mutated batarians that consume corpses to grow armor); harvesters (30-to-40-foot flying gunships and transports); marauders (transformed turians acting as battlefield leaders); brutes (turian-krogan hybrids); ravagers (mutated rachni used as living artillery); banshees (corrupted asari with powerful biotics); the Oculus (a fast flying drone used by Reapers and Collectors); and swarmers (tiny, numerous drones).
evidence.for_key: densorin oravores Reapers

codex.text: - Victory was a Prothean VI overseer of an Eden Prime bunker during the Reaper invasion 50,000 years ago; it forced base commander Javik into stasis and triggered a neutron bombardment that destroyed the Reaper threat but crippled the base, eventually cutting power to every stasis pod except Javik's and naming him the voice of his people (source: Victory).

- Known VIs included the Prothean VIs Vigil (Ilos), Vendetta (Thessia), and Victory (Eden Prime), the Shadow Broker's Glyph, the quarian Ancestor VI Liat'Nir, and the Andromeda ark VI "K" (source: Virtual Intelligence).
